scope: src/main.js lines 37723-38218 (buildMegaplexB01Map level controller: room visibility, managed lights, zone doors, dynamic props) + 38647-38754 (TRAINING RANGE start/tick) + 41320-41551 (VIS_DEBUG overlays, post isolation, material override). Adjacent context read: 37700-37722 (B01 map config), 41552-41575 (frame loop now=seconds), 23425-23440 (_applyShadowQuality shadowCasters consumer).

findings.title: Megaplex B01 level casts ZERO shadows — directional key light has castShadow=false and is never registered as a shadow caster
findings.description: The only level-wide light that could cast a sun/key shadow is the DirectionalLight `key`. It is built with `key.castShadow=false`, a full 2048x2048 shadow camera is then configured (all dead config), and `key` is pushed into `ceilingLights` but NOT into the `shadowCasters` array. The `shadowCasters` array (declared line 37733) is returned (line 38207) but is NEVER pushed to anywhere in this builder, so it is always empty. All GLB point lights are also forced `object.castShadow=false` (line 37875). `_applyShadowQuality()` (line 23431-23435) only toggles castShadow on lights in `levelData.shadowCasters`, so even with shadow quality on High the megaplex renders completely shadowless. The whole loading-dock megaplex therefore looks flat/CG with no grounding contact shadows — the single biggest 'not AAA' tell on load. Compare buildAimDemoMap (line 38314-38319) which sets key.castShadow=true and pushes key into shadowCasters.
findings.evidence: const key=new THREE.DirectionalLight(0xffd49a,.95); ... key.castShadow=false; key.shadow.mapSize.set(2048,2048); key.shadow.camera.left=-75;...; localObjects.push(key,key.target);ceilingLights.push(key);  // shadowCasters[] declared at 37733 but never pushed; returned empty at 38207
findings.fix: Set `key.castShadow=true` (the shadow camera is already sized -75..75 / -135..135 near 1 far 180, covering the level) and add `shadowCasters.push(key);` right after the existing `localObjects.push(key,key.target);ceilingLights.push(key);` line. This lets `_applyShadowQuality` enable/disable it per quality setting and gives the level real directional shadows. Keep point lights non-shadow-casting for perf.
findings.risk: Shadow rendering perf cost on this large level. Mitigated because _applyShadowQuality gates castShadow by SETTINGS.shadowQuality/quality (off on low). Confirm static probes don't assert shadowCasters.length===0 for this map; visualStats already advertises csmSplits:0 so a single shadowed directional is consistent. Does not touch save data.

findings.title: Directional key light (and hemi/ambient) get added to pulseLights and have their intensity modulated every frame
findings.description: `pulseLights=ceilingLights.map(l=>({l,base:l.intensity||1,...}))` (line 38022) is built from `ceilingLights`, which includes the DirectionalLight key (37997), the HemisphereLight (37985) and the AmbientLight (37988) in addition to the GLB point lights. The tickDynProps pulse loop (38168-38176) then multiplies EVERY one of those by `base*(1+sin*amp)` each frame. The intent of pulseLights is clearly to flicker room/alarm point lights, not the global sun/fill. Today amp is only .06 so it's barely visible, but once shadows are enabled on the key light (see megaplex-no-shadows-flat) the entire scene's directional shadows and exposure will visibly shimmer at ~1.3Hz, and the hemi/ambient fill will breathe — an unintended global flicker.
findings.fix: Build pulseLights only from point lights / room lights, e.g. `const pulseLights=ceilingLights.filter(l=>l&&l.isPointLight).map(...)`, or skip non-point lights inside the loop with `if(!p.l.isPointLight)continue;`. This isolates the flicker to room/alarm point lights and keeps the key/fill stable.
findings.risk: Behavioral: hemi/ambient/key stop pulsing (desired). No save/perf impact. Low risk.

findings.title: Zone-door gate-id regex uses \\. (literal backslash) instead of \. so the float-formatted '.0' suffix never matches
findings.description: In b01MegaplexZoneDoorIndexFor the two regex literals `/mega_zone_gate_22(?:\\.0)?_/` and `/mega_zone_gate_-22(?:\\.0)?_/` are clearly trying to optionally match a float-formatted coordinate '22.0'. Inside a regex literal, `\\.` is a LITERAL backslash followed by any-char, not an escaped dot. So the group `(?:\\.0)?` matches '\<anychar>0', never '.0'. A gate whose id is e.g. 'mega_zone_gate_22.0_left' will fail this test. The two other paths (explicit ud.zoneDoorIndex, and the closed_zone_gate positional z>=0 fallback) usually mask this, so it is a latent bug: a gate part that relies solely on the gateId pattern (no zoneDoorIndex, floorplanRole != 'closed_zone_gate') will return null and not be registered as a lift door, so it would not animate open / would not become a navigable opening.
findings.fix: Replace `\\.` with `\.`: `/mega_zone_gate_22(?:\.0)?_/` and `/mega_zone_gate_-22(?:\.0)?_/`. (Single backslash-dot to match a literal period.)
findings.risk: Could newly match gate ids that previously fell through to the positional fallback; behavior should be equivalent or more correct. Verify gate ids actually contain '22.0' formatting; if they only ever use integer '22' the optional group is simply moot and the fix is harmless.

findings.title: tickDynProps unit-normalization heuristic and default param disagree on units (fragile, currently masked)
findings.description: tickDynProps signature is `(dt,now=performance.now())` and immediately does `const nowMs=now>100000?now:now*1000;`. The sole live call site (line 43950) passes the frame loop's `now`, which is `performance.now()*0.001` (SECONDS). For seconds input the heuristic uses `now*1000` (correct ms) and only breaks after ~100000s (~27.7h) uptime. But the DEFAULT parameter `performance.now()` is MILLISECONDS: if tickDynProps were ever called with no `now` argument during the first 100s of page life, `now<100000` would be true and `nowMs=now*1000` would be 1000x too large, instantly desyncing the room/light cull throttles (260ms/180ms) and the pulse phase `t=nowMs*.0025`. The magnitude-sniffing of units is brittle and the default param is inconsistent with the only caller.
findings.fix: Make units explicit. Either change the default to seconds: `now=performance.now()*0.001` and always do `const nowMs=now*1000;`, or drop the heuristic and require callers to pass seconds. Removing the `>100000` branch eliminates the ~27.7h overflow edge too.
findings.risk: None for the live caller (already seconds). Pure robustness hardening. Verify no other code path calls tickDynProps with ms.

findings.title: Megaplex base lighting is very dim/flat (hemi .42, ambient .18, key .95, no shadows) and point lights hard-capped to 3 visible
findings.description: The runtime base lights for the megaplex are HemisphereLight .42, AmbientLight .18, DirectionalLight key .95 (and the key casts no shadow per megaplex-no-shadows-flat). On top of that, updateManagedLights (38116-38123) hard-caps to `cap=3` visible point lights within a 52m radius, and each GLB point light intensity was already crushed to `Math.min(1.55,Math.max(.18,intensity*.006))` (line 37877). Net result is a uniformly dim, low-contrast, low-key-fill scene with almost no local pools of light — reads as flat/unfinished rather than the moody high-contrast look the rest of the project targets. This compounds the missing shadows.
findings.evidence: const hemi=new THREE.HemisphereLight(0x9fb8d4,0x17130f,.42); ... const ambient=new THREE.AmbientLight(0x8190a0,.18); ... const key=new THREE.DirectionalLight(0xffd49a,.95); ... const cap=3,hard=52*52;
findings.fix: Cheap visible win: bump the key DirectionalLight to ~1.6-2.2 and enable its shadow (see megaplex-no-shadows-flat) for directional grounding, and raise the managed-light `cap` from 3 to ~5-6 (still budgeted) so room pools of light are visible as the player moves. Optionally raise per-point-light floor from .18. Keep hemi/ambient low so the key/point contrast reads. All values are tunable constants; no structural change.
findings.risk: Lighting/perf tuning — raising cap adds active point lights (still bounded by distance hard=52^2). Validate against visualStats/light-budget probes which advertise realPointLights:managedRoomLights.length. Avoid exceeding the 12-light triage threshold in _perfTriage (line 41536). Medium confidence on exact numbers; direction is sound.

findings.title: Training-range target dummies are pushed directly into enemyMgr._list and reset by hand-poking bMesh/hMesh y positions
findings.description: startRange creates dummies via `new Enemy(...)` and pushes them straight into `G.enemyMgr._list` (line 38700), bypassing the manager's spawn path. tickRange respawns dead dummies by directly writing `t.bMesh.position.y=.76; t.hMesh.position.y=1.48; t.group.scale.setScalar(1); t.group.rotation.set(0,0,0)` and manually walking materials to reset opacity/transparent (38713-38728). This duplicates whatever the Enemy class's own spawn/reset does and will silently desync if the Enemy rig's rest-pose y offsets, group scale, or death-fade material handling ever change (e.g. an enemy whose hMesh rest y is not 1.48, or with extra meshes that fade). At timeout it sets t.removeNeeded=true on directly-injected list members, relying on the manager's removeNeeded sweep to dispose them.
findings.fix: Prefer a manager-owned spawn/reset API (e.g. enemyMgr.spawnDummy / enemy.resetToSpawn) so the rest pose, scale and material-fade reset live in one place. If kept inline, read the rest y offsets from the Enemy instance (capture them at spawn) instead of hardcoding .76/1.48 so it can't drift from the rig.
findings.risk: Refactor touches range mode only (secondary mode). Low visible impact today; this is drift-resistance. Don't change hardcoded values blindly without confirming current rig offsets.

findings.title: _setMaterialOverride sets scene.overrideMaterial globally with no scene-change/cleanup reset
findings.description: _setMaterialOverride assigns `scene.overrideMaterial` (clay/normal/wire), which three.js applies to EVERY mesh in the scene including the first-person viewmodel, muzzle/tracer/decal VFX and any 3D HUD elements, and it survives a level change (it is never reset in cleanup() or on quitToMain). It is a dev-only debug entry (exposed via installPerfDebug setMaterialOverride at 45896), so impact is contained to debug usage, but a forgotten 'wire'/'clay' override persists across deploys and would make the whole game render in debug material until manually cleared. The cached overrideMats are also never disposed (minor, intentional cache).
findings.evidence: scene.overrideMaterial=VIS_DEBUG.overrideMats[next];  // never reset on cleanup / level change; affects viewmodel+VFX+HUD meshes too
findings.fix: Optional hardening: reset `scene.overrideMaterial=null` (and VIS_DEBUG.materialOverride='none') inside level cleanup / quitToMain, or restrict the override to the level root rather than the whole scene. Low priority since it is debug-only, but cheap to guard.
findings.risk: Debug-only path; change is low risk. Don't dispose the cached override materials if you want re-toggle to stay instant.

findings.title: Dead shadow-camera configuration on a non-shadow-casting megaplex key light
findings.description: Because `key.castShadow=false`, the immediately following `key.shadow.mapSize.set(2048,2048)` and the full `key.shadow.camera` left/right/top/bottom/near/far setup are dead — they allocate/configure a shadow camera that is never used. This is harmless but is a clear signal the key light was intended to cast shadows and the castShadow flag is the contradiction (tracks with megaplex-no-shadows-flat).
findings.fix: Resolve together with megaplex-no-shadows-flat by flipping castShadow to true (making the config live) and registering the light in shadowCasters; otherwise the shadow config can be deleted as dead.
findings.risk: None on its own. Resolving via enabling shadows carries the perf consideration noted in megaplex-no-shadows-flat.
